keyDisagreements: Binary gates vs Ben's real keeps. Four members wanted the grader's kill-shape list (résumé, lawsuit, debunk-led, grim, trademark, doorless) as hard bounces; the Devil's Advocate re-scored the 26 positives against that text and found 5–6 of Ben's 15 kept rows and 1 used row fail it (Littlefeather, Superman ice cream, Duracell, St. Valentine's, Devo; Frank Oz on résumé). Nobody rebutted the numbers — the rebuttals were about door typing on old rows, which is a formatting artifact, not the same point. Ruling: only the four clusters with zero counter-examples stay binary (unsayable answer, lawsuit-as-the-fact, mined vein, unverified); the rest score with kept-vs-killed anchor pairs. Second disagreement: new files (templates, generator-common) vs trim in place. Ruled for templates on the "violated three times" evidence, but capped at three new files and one deletion. Ship order if time is short: changes 1–7 (grade mode, live §5, §9 exemplars, Phase 1 cut, §0 as the gate list, grader rewrite) are what run one needs; templates, generator-common and the format-library cut can follow the first `/fact-hunt quick 30`.
devilsAdvocateImpact: Yes — he changed the final call in two places. (1) The grader: his verdict-row audit is the only quantitative check anyone ran on today's rewrite, and it showed the new binary gates bounce a third of Ben's positives while a mandated 30–60% bounce rate would report that as health. The ruling drops debunk-led/grim/trademark/door/résumé from the binary list and deletes the re-run-until-it-bounces rule. His Frank Oz catch also exposed an in-file contradiction the majority missed. (2) Phase 1: the majority wanted the corpus study replaced by a pinned doc; his point that "doc over bank" is what produced this morning's "real-world nearly absent" error kept one cheap live tag-count as a drift check. His fame-grep, lane-only allocation, `--deep` flag and no-new-files positions were rejected on the merits.
